# v3.14

A single security-hardening change, rolling up the one dev pre-release since
v3.13 (**v3.14-dev**). Nothing looks or behaves differently, and no action is
needed on your side.

## What changed

**Forced two-factor enrolment is now enforced in two independent places instead
of one.**

When an administrator requires a user to set up two-factor authentication, that
user is held on the setup page until they finish. Until now a single component
was responsible for holding them there, and the roughly fifty data endpoints
behind it trusted that it had already done its job.

Each of those endpoints now checks for itself. Two supporting endpoints are
covered by the same fix — the background keep-alive that stops an idle session
expiring, and the change-password endpoint. The keep-alive was the one that
mattered: without it, a session partway through a required setup could keep
renewing its own idle timer instead of lapsing.

**Nothing changes in normal use.** The setup page behaves exactly as before, a
user who completes setup gets access immediately as they always did, and
sign-out remains available throughout. What changes is that a fault or a gap in
that one component can no longer expose data to a half-enrolled session on its
own.

## How it was checked

The first protective layer was deliberately switched off, and requests that
previously succeeded for a half-enrolled session were confirmed to be refused.
A complete enrolment — sign in, scan, enter a code, gain access — was then run
from start to finish to confirm the normal path is untouched. An independent
review of the change repeated both, and widened them: it found two further
endpoints that needed the same treatment, which are included here.

## Upgrading

No action required. Users partway through a required two-factor setup are
unaffected.
